arml-2012-superrelay-01.title: Make y large
arml-2012-superrelay-01.body:
$y$ divides $\gcd(20,12)=4$, and $x=\frac{20}y$, $z=\frac{12}y$, so $x+z=\frac{32}{y}$ is smallest when $y=4$: $x=5$, $z=3$, $x+z=8$.

**Answer: 8**

arml-2012-superrelay-02.title: Equidistant point
arml-2012-superrelay-02.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 1, which is 8.)*


$B=(7,17)$. A point on the perpendicular bisector is equidistant from $A$ and $B$:
$$(x-1)^2+(3-5)^2=(x-7)^2+(3-17)^2\implies -2x+1+4=-14x+49+196\implies 12x=240.$$
So $x=20$.

**Answer: 20**

arml-2012-superrelay-02.title: Slope form
arml-2012-superrelay-02.body:
The midpoint of $AB$ is $(4,11)$ and the slope of $AB$ is $\frac{12}{6}=2$, so the bisector is $y-11=-\frac12(x-4)$. Setting $y=3$: $x-4=16$, $x=20$.

**Answer: 20**

arml-2012-superrelay-03.title: Divisibility by 3 and 11
arml-2012-superrelay-03.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 2, which is 20.)*


$N=10\ldots0\,\underline{a}\,\underline{b}$ should be as small as possible. Try $N=10^{19}+m$ with small $m$. $N$ must have digit sum divisible by 3 and alternating digit sum divisible by 11. With only the leading 1 and the last two digits nonzero: counting positions from the right starting at $0$, the leading 1 of a 20-digit number is in position 19 (odd), so the alternating sum is $b-a-1$, which (being between $-10$ and $8$) must be $0$: $b=a+1$. The digit sum $1+a+b=2a+2$ must be divisible by 3, so the smallest choice is $a=2$, $b=3$: $N=10\ldots023$.

The product of the last two digits is $2\cdot3=6$.

**Answer: 6**

arml-2012-superrelay-03.title: Direct computation
arml-2012-superrelay-03.body:
$10^{19}\equiv 10\pmod{33}$ (since $100\equiv1$), so the smallest multiple of 33 that is at least $10^{19}$ is $10^{19}+23$. Its last two digits are $2,3$, with product $6$.

**Answer: 6**

arml-2012-superrelay-04.title: Trapezoid with midlines
arml-2012-superrelay-04.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 3, which is 6.)*


$DESH$ is a trapezoid with parallel sides $DE=T$ and $SH$, and height $\frac T2$.

$AS$ is a midline of $\triangle EFM$ (it joins the midpoint $A$ of $EF$ to a point of $EM$, parallel to $FM$), so $AS=\frac12FM=\frac T6$; similarly $BH=\frac T6$. Hence $SH=T-\frac{2T}6=\frac{2T}3$ and
$$[DESH]=\frac12\left(T+\frac{2T}3\right)\cdot\frac T2=\frac{5T^2}{12}=\frac{5\cdot36}{12}=15.$$

**Answer: 15**

arml-2012-superrelay-05.title: Alternate z and its conjugate
arml-2012-superrelay-05.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 4, which is 15.)*


$f_n(z)=z$ for odd $n$ and $\overline z$ for even $n$. With $z=a+bi$:
$$(1+3+5)z+(2+4)\overline z=9(a+bi)+6(a-bi)=15a+3bi=T+Ti.$$
So $a=\frac T{15}=1$, $b=\frac T3=5$, and $|z|=\sqrt{1+25}=\sqrt{26}$.

**Answer: $\sqrt{26}$**

arml-2012-superrelay-06.title: Each prime goes to one side
arml-2012-superrelay-06.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 5, which is $\sqrt{26}$.)*


If $\gcd(a,b)=1$, each prime power in the factorisation of $ab$ goes entirely to $a$ or entirely to $b$; with $k$ distinct primes there are $2^k$ ordered pairs.

$T^{20}\cdot210^{12}=26^{10}\cdot210^{12}=2^{22}\cdot3^{12}\cdot5^{12}\cdot7^{12}\cdot13^{10}$ has $5$ distinct primes, giving $2^5=32$ pairs.

**Answer: 32**

arml-2012-superrelay-07.title: Geometric series
arml-2012-superrelay-07.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 6, which is 32.)*


$\cos^2\theta=1-\frac{T^2-64}{T^2}=\frac{64}{T^2}$, so $\cos\theta=\pm\frac8{32}=\pm\frac14$. The series $\frac{\cos\theta}{1-\cos\theta}$ is larger for $\cos\theta=\frac14$: $\frac{1/4}{3/4}=\frac13$.

**Answer: $\frac13$**

arml-2012-superrelay-08.title: Common external tangent
arml-2012-superrelay-08.body:
*(In the Super Relay, problem 8 received two numbers: $\frac13$, the answer to problem 7, and $450$, the answer to problem 9; $R$ is the larger and $r$ the smaller.)*

$DY$ and $KP$ are both perpendicular to the tangent line. Drop the perpendicular from $K$ to $DY$ with foot $J$; then $PKJY$ is a rectangle, $DJ=R-r$, and $DK=R+r$ (the circles are externally tangent). So
$$YP=JK=\sqrt{(R+r)^2-(R-r)^2}=2\sqrt{Rr}=2\sqrt{150}=10\sqrt6.$$

**Answer: $10\sqrt6$**

arml-2012-superrelay-09.title: Pythagoras to the center
arml-2012-superrelay-09.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 10, which is $\frac{9}{17}$.)*


The foot of the altitude is the centre of the square, so half the diagonal is $\sqrt{n^2-(n-m)^2}=\sqrt{2mn-m^2}$. The area of a square is half the square of its diagonal: $\frac12\cdot4(2mn-m^2)=4mn-2m^2$.

With $m=9$, $n=17$: $612-162=450$.

**Answer: 450**

arml-2012-superrelay-10.title: Only the second person can be a Leo
arml-2012-superrelay-10.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 11, which is $-14$.)*


$d=14$. The woman was born on July 1–13, so she is not a Leo. The man was born on one of July 15–31 (17 equally likely days), and he is a Leo for July 23–31 (9 days). So the probability is $\frac9{17}$.

**Answer: $\frac{9}{17}$**

arml-2012-superrelay-11.title: Simplify the logs
arml-2012-superrelay-11.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 12, which is $-10$.)*


$\log_2 4^{8!}=2\cdot8!$ and $\log_4 2^{8!}=\frac{8!}2$, so the left side is $\frac52\cdot8!=\frac52\cdot56\cdot6!=140\cdot6!$. Thus $Tx=140$ and $x=\frac{140}{-10}=-14$.

**Answer: $-14$**

arml-2012-superrelay-12.title: Match coefficients
arml-2012-superrelay-12.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 13, which is 20.)*


Divide the second equation by 2: $x^2+\left(\frac T2+4a-1\right)x+5b=0$, versus $x^2+(5b-T-a)x-(T+1)=0$. Monic quadratics with the same solution set have the same coefficients, so
$$5b=-(T+1),\qquad 5b-T-a=\frac T2+4a-1.$$
Substituting, $-2T-1-a=\frac T2+4a-1$, so $5a=-\frac{5T}2$ and $a=-\frac T2=-10$.

(With $T=20$, $b=-\frac{21}5$, and both equations become $x^2+9x-21=0$, which has two real roots.)

**Answer: $-10$**

arml-2012-superrelay-13.title: Rate per worker
arml-2012-superrelay-13.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 14, which is 14.)*


$K=12$. One worker makes $\frac9K$ widgets per hour, so $\frac{36}K$ widgets in 4 hours. To make $\frac{720}K$ widgets in 4 hours we need $\frac{720/K}{36/K}=20$ workers (for any $K$).

**Answer: 20**

arml-2012-superrelay-14.title: Alternating digit sum
arml-2012-superrelay-14.body:
*(In the Super Relay, $T$ was the answer to problem 15, which is 2018.)*


The number is $\underline{2}\,\underline{0}\,\underline{1}\,\underline{8}\,\underline{A}\,\underline{A}\,\underline{B}=2018\cdot1000+\underline{AAB}$. Since $1000\equiv-1\pmod{11}$ and $\underline{AAB}=110A+B\equiv B$, the number is $\equiv B-2018\equiv B-5\pmod{11}$ (as $2018=11\cdot183+5$). So $B=5$, and $A$ is free; take $A=9$: $A+B=14$.

**Answer: 14**

arml-2012-superrelay-15.title: Count weekday shifts
arml-2012-superrelay-15.body:
From one April 1 to the next the weekday advances by 1 (365 days) or by 2 if the following February has a 29th (366 days). From 2012: 2013 Monday, 2014 Tuesday, 2015 Wednesday, 2016 Friday (leap year), 2017 Saturday, 2018 Sunday.

**Answer: 2018**
